definitions.gloss: to install, to set up, to back (as leader)
definitions.explanation: To elevate or install someone in a position of authority, especially as a political leader, party head, or figurehead. Implies that a group collectively supports and puts forward a person for a leadership role.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{党首|とうしゅ}を{擁立|ようりつ}した。
examples.english: They installed a new party leader.

examples.japanese: {野党|やとう}は{独自|どくじ}の{候補者|こうほしゃ}を{擁立|ようりつ}する{方針|ほうしん}だ。
examples.english: The opposition party plans to put forward its own candidate.

examples.japanese: {各|かく}{派閥|はばつ}がそれぞれの{候補|こうほ}を{擁立|ようりつ}し、{党内|とうない}の{対立|たいりつ}が{深|ふか}まった。
examples.english: Each faction put forward its own candidate, deepening the divisions within the party.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Used as a する verb: {擁立|ようりつ}する. Takes を to mark the person being installed: ～を{擁立|ようりつ}する.

USAGE:
A political and historical term. Most commonly seen in news coverage of elections, leadership contests, and party politics. In historical contexts, it describes the installation of emperors, shoguns, or other rulers by powerful supporters.

The word implies that the person being installed has the backing of a group or faction, rather than achieving the position entirely on their own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {候補者|こうほしゃ}を{擁立|ようりつ}する: to put forward a candidate
- {党首|とうしゅ}を{擁立|ようりつ}する: to install a party leader
- {対立|たいりつ}{候補|こうほ}を{擁立|ようりつ}: to put up a rival candidate
